Master Fazhen was endowed with innate genius that preceded his time,
and his talent stood far above the world.
Having firmly mastered its essential meaning, he then...

He delved into the profound mystery; it was not for his own private benefit, but truly with the desire to establish a public standard for ten thousand generations in order to remedy the prevailing defects.
Thus, he preserved [this work] deeply.
I have long contemplated this.
By employing his strategies, he has brought the Huayan school to its great perfection. I, Xidi, am not gifted; yet I have studied and practiced it, briefly analyzing [its principles].
Regarding these profound and subtle matters, I have ventured to offer this brief commentary.
Although it offers no benefit to the Teaching, my sincere application of mind has reached its limit. I hope you will not hold me culpable for this.
On the first day of the first month of the second year of the Jiatai era,
Xidi respectfully prefaces this work on the One Vehicle of the Shared Teaching of the Avatamsaka Sūtra,
composed by Dharma Master Zhuzhuan Shenzhu, Shi Huihui.

Question: Regarding the Great Vehicle of the Avataṃsaka, there are only the two teachings of the identical and the distinct. [Tài] says: "As for the meaning of the One Vehicle, it is distinguished as twofold: first, the direct vehicle; second, the provisional vehicle, and so forth."

The commentary states: This means that the vehicle is of two kinds, and the teaching establishes two gates; therefore, it is said that they are "only identical or distinct. Regarding the meaning of "distinct," the explanations are mostly identical (where "identical" refers to the single distinct teaching).

However, [the principle of] ease and simplicity is particularly exceptional, yet it is often not followed. (Regarding the unique explanation of ease and simplicity as being able to propagate the distinctions among the three types of doctrinal gates, the reason it is "often not followed" is as Yangzi said:

"That which does not accord with the laws of the former kings, the gentleman does not take as a model. If the identical teaching has a single meaning, some say there are three types. (This is precisely "ease and simplicity. As for saying there are three types: first, the fusion of the identical.)

"Second, the identity of the union; third, the identity of the meaning. Some say there are four gates (referring to the *Huìjiě*: first, the identity of the union of three and one; second, the identity of the merging of the two vehicles; third, the identity of similar categories of meaning; fourth, the identity of accomplishing a single teaching).

It is said that while there are minor differences, the great meaning does not diverge. (Yí'ān says: "Shànzhù refers to himself. If this is so, then because he identifies with that 'convergence of the three,' it is called 'minor difference';

because the essential intent is one, it is called 'non-divergence'"). Yet students are divided, not knowing which is correct. I request the young men of talent to consult the patriarchs extensively and choose [the right path].

The text indicates the destination to which one returns: one should adjudicate right and wrong through public discourse and must not privately favor one's own faction. My most sincere wishes! My most sincere wishes! Regarding the phrase "one word universally encompasses" (*yī yán tōng mù*):

the internal commentary states that "furthermore, regarding 'sameness' (*tóng*), there are many distinct meanings. One word [universally] encompasses what is contained within a given stage (*wèi*). This refers to how it universally encompasses the stages of understanding, practice, and so forth. It takes a single meaning according to the specific context.

The internal commentary further says: "The meanings brought together are not identical; there are many kinds of dharma-gates. One takes a single meaning according to the specific case, while the others have no distinct characteristics [in that regard]; therefore, they are said to be the same. The commentary explains: The *Dilun* (Treatise on the Stages) says:

From the stage of faith up to the Bodhisattvas who share a single *pratītyasamutpāda* with the inconceivable Buddha-dharmas, the meanings of identity and difference are each explained within both the "identical" and "distinctive" [teachings].

(Regarding the explanation of identity and difference: it is said that within the Distinctive Teaching (*biejiao*) there is also identity and difference. That many are identical to one is its identity; that one is manifested as many is its difference. Within the Identical Teaching (*tongjiao*) there is likewise identity and difference. That the One Vehicle and the Three Vehicles share the same skillful means is their identity;
that they are distinguished according to the capacities of sentient beings is their difference. These are not points of contention among various quarters and need not be debated.
The first section of this chapter concerns the distinct teaching (biejiao), and the second concerns the common teaching (tongjiao). Yi Jian’s commentary states:

"In the subsequent section on the common teaching, one directly addresses the fundamental and derivative aspects of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) as being harmoniously integrated. Therefore, the following section says: 'This common teaching explains that all vehicles and so forth are interfused and non-dual, being one and the same dharma-realm.'"

The critique states: The citations presented here are incomplete (as it subsequently says, "there are two gates," etc.). Furthermore, the thesis (*pakṣa*) and the reason (*hetu*) are confused (taking the thesis as the reason).

Therefore, it is said that this is a confusion, as in the analogy of burning firewood. [The author] himself claims, "This is the gate for propagating [the teaching], not the teaching intended for those of specific capacities.

If one truly understands the unity and diversity within the Flower Store World (Huāzàng), one will certainly not go beyond these words. As the Book of Documents says: "If the net is on the main rope, there will be order and no disorder."
Welcoming Blessings (Yingfu) comments: "This is an exposition that unifies the three and the one;

thus, the Three Vehicles and the One Vehicle are harmonized and not distinct. He further notes: "This refers to their identity based on the possession of both the three and the one. Furthermore, it distinguishes this from the sea possessing the hundred rivers [as a metaphor for totality], and so forth...

(The *Huìjiě* commentary states: "Because the first meaning possesses the three and the one vehicle, it differs slightly from 'total inclusion. Since total inclusion must refer to the sea possessing the hundred rivers, it is said to differ slightly. Because it possesses the three and the one, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* is classified as a teaching of sameness (*tóngjiào*).")

Zhixiang’s commentary states: The Sūtra says, "The three are unified and return to the One," and therefore they are identical. (Question: Regarding the second chapter on "Re-entering [the Teaching]," it says that "uniting the three and returning to the one" refers to the characteristics of the teaching.)

How could this be intended as an explanation of the same character? Now, [the author] says: "Regarding the *Zhixiang* [commentary], it asks: 'Why? The answer is: This refers to the explanation of the meaning (*yì*), while that refers to the explanation of the text (*wén*); they do not contradict one another.

There are many such instances of multiple meanings, as in the "Chapter on the Sublime Meaning" (*Miaozu Zhang*). Furthermore, it says: "Now, seeking a comprehensive understanding through principle, there are both common and distinct approaches.

Here, we follow the *Zhixiang*. (As Mencius said: "What I wish for is to study Confucius," and again: "I have not yet been able to become a disciple of Confucius; I have privately cultivated myself through others.")

The critique states: *Yìjiǎn* takes that "distinct teaching" (*biéjiào*) and contrasts it with this "identity within distinction. (*Yìjiǎn* says: "The Chapter on the Sublime Meaning" states that it is called the 'distinct teaching' because it is distinct from the three vehicles.
Now, by taking that identity, we demonstrate the identity within the contrast to the distinct; thus, the meaning is not erroneous. (The Master [Zhiyi] personally stated:

"The meaning is abundant and [has been] codified; the analogical explanations are most appropriate. Yíngfú also said: "If the meanings of the distinct are all identical, then they are also the same. (*Huìjiě*, fascicle 8, states: "The name 'distinct teaching'...")
The meaning [of these terms] is the same for all the Patriarchs. “With” (yǔ) signifies permission; as the saying goes: “I permit you to say that I am not their equal.
In the *Qīngliáng zǒngxiàng huìtōng* (Clear Cool Compendium of General Correlations), it is sometimes divided into four [categories], stating:

third is the *sāmānya-śāsana ekayāna* (common teaching of the One Vehicle), such as the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and others (*Dà jīng shù*, fascicle 2, states: “The three intermediate teachings preserve the three and subsume the two; therefore, they are opened into four: first, the *pratyeka-śāsana hīnayāna*, such as the *Catur-āgama* and others; second, the *sāmānya-śāsana triyāna*, such as the *Śrīmālā-sūtra*...”).

1. The Esoteric [Vehicle], etc.; 2. The One Vehicle of Common Teaching (*sādhāraṇa-ekayāna*), such as the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and others; 3. The One Vehicle of Distinct Teaching (*prātideśanika-ekayāna*), such as the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra* and others.
In the section on "Subsuming and Benefiting" within the *Yìjiǎn Shèjiào Zhāng*, it states regarding the One Vehicle of Common Teaching:

"This is the synthesis of the Three Vehicles and the One Vehicle, and thus belongs to the category of the Common Teaching. The aforementioned One Vehicle of Distinct Teaching is the Perfect Teaching (*yuanjiao*); the Three Vehicles of the Provisional Teachings [belong to the former]."
This refers to the Initial Teaching (śāstra). The One Vehicle of the Shared Teaching corresponds to the Final and Sudden Teachings.

Thus, the *Weixin jueyi lun xuanyi* (Profound Meaning of the Treatise on Resolving Ignorance) states: "The three [teachings] of the shared one vehicle are like the *Lotus Sūtra*. The *Yanyi* (Exegesis) commentary explains: "This combines the two teachings of the Final and the Sudden.

(The shared teaching is singular, yet its manifestations are manifold; this is surely for the sake of gathering and benefiting beings. Among the five teachings, the first four correspond to the Three Vehicles, while the last one corresponds to the Distinct Teaching. The harmonious integration of these three and one constitutes the shared teaching. To now categorize it into four—how much error there is!)
The critique states: This master further points out that this is precisely what the Separate Teaching (biejiao) does not exclude.

(Yi Jian says: The Final and Sudden Teachings are also the One Vehicle; they are not excluded by this. He further states: Although the texts of the Final and Sudden Teachings do not exclude them, they are always fundamentally distinct from it. (Next, he says:)

Because the *Avataṃsaka* alone possesses the virtue of perfect interpenetration (*yuanrong*), it is divided into three categories within the subsequent section on the "Inclusion and Benefits of Doctrinal Meanings": first, the Separate Teaching of the One Vehicle; second, the Provisional Teaching of the Three Vehicles; and third, the Common Teaching of the One Vehicle.

This differs from the Final and Sudden [teachings] (hence it is pointed out here that this corresponds to the Final and Sudden, and is not the Perfect Teaching). Within the "Decisive Determination of Its Meaning," it is also stated that the Final and Sudden are not the latter teaching.
Other meanings are not recorded here. (The phrase "this corresponds to" etc., indicates that the gate of teaching and the aspect of meaning are two distinct things.)
The *Yingfu hui jie* states: "Because the two teachings—the Final and the Sudden—equally eliminate duality, they are termed the 'One Vehicle of the Identical Teaching' (*tongjiao yicheng*).

The commentary notes: "This refers to the elimination of duality within the Final and Sudden teachings; it does not mean that the Final and Sudden teachings themselves are combined to constitute the identical teaching."

This is precisely because the Final and Sudden [teachings] are equally devoid of the Two Vehicles; therefore, they are called the "Common Teaching of the One Vehicle. Furthermore, in the commentary on the subsequent section, it says:

"If the self-characteristics of the Final and Sudden were identical, yet the Gradual and Sudden differ, how could they be the same? It further states: "It is not that the Final and Sudden are combined to constitute 'sameness';
rather, they are named 'common' because they equally eliminate duality. It also says: "People of recent times all say that the Final..."
"To combine the sudden and the two teachings [of the gradual] as a single 'identical teaching' (tóngjiào) while the gradual and the sudden remain distinct—how can they be combined?

(*Huìjiě*, Fascicle 8). The critique states: "This is neither the 'identical' within the Perfect [Teaching], nor is it a combination of the Final and the Sudden; rather, it is the existence and disappearance resulting from their separation.
Furthermore, taking the merging of these two as the reason for naming it the 'Identical Teaching' is incorrect. (The above establishes its fallacy; the remainder follows.)
The meaning can be understood as it was analyzed during the lecture.

As the Qingliang commentary states: "Because the Initial Teaching maintains the three [vehicles], it is established as a separate teaching; because the Final and Sudden Teachings dissolve these two into one, they are the same."

These are combined into a single teaching. As stated in the following section on the four [teachings]: "The third is the One Vehicle of the Common Teaching (*sādhāraṇa-yāna*), which combines the Final and Sudden Teachings" (Yanyi Chao, fascicle 6).

The critique states: This is the merging of the two [distinctions] into identity; it is the reason for bringing them forth together as a single teaching. (The words and meanings are radiant; the thesis and its reasons are fully appropriate. Qingliang said:

"When Zhongni [Confucius] encountered [Zizhang], they shared their carriage; when Boya [stopped playing] his strings, he did so because of the resonance of form and sound. To transmit without meeting face-to-face and to grasp the essential meaning beyond the manifest—this intention is as my own heart;

I do not know if such a thing exists. It is not the cause by which this teaching derives its name. (How could a son of the Zhang family become a son of the Li family? Nevertheless, the criticism of being a mere superficial reader cannot be avoided. Therefore, it remains."
The three [teachings] are unified into one teaching; the two [extremes] are merged into one teaching. Together with the Small [Vehicle] and the Perfect [Vehicle], there are four.

This is also clearly stated as the "One Vehicle of the Same Teaching," which combines the Final and the Sudden [teachings]. This differs from [the system of] Yingfu. The author’s own commentary states:

"Nevertheless, each establishes its own position independently; one need not harbor doubts regarding this. (This refers to the fact that Qingliang’s establishment of the system differs from that of Yingfu.)

It is further stated: "Based on whether they are harmoniously integrated (*yuanrong*) or not, two types are distinguished. That is, both the True Teaching (*shijiao*) and the Sudden Teaching (*dunjiao*) are non-integrated, and thus constitute the One Vehicle of the Shared Teaching (*tongjiao yicheng*).

(Zhenyuan I, Part 1). Shanzhu’s own commentary states: "This is based on the non-obstruction between principle and phenomenon (*lishi wuai*), serving as a distinction from the non-obstruction between phenomena themselves (*shishi wuai*).
Question: "If [the True and Sudden Teachings] are entirely non-integrated, how do they differ from the Sudden and True [Vehicles]? Answer: "If one enters..."

[The teaching] is perfectly subsumed. There is the non-obstruction between principle and phenomena (*dharmatā-dharma*). There must be the non-obstruction of phenomena. Why? Because the four gates, such as "manifesting its non-obstruction," are all distinct teachings (*pṛthag-deśanā*).

(The *Xuánwén* states: "Now, to reveal the One Vehicle of the distinct teaching, four gates are briefly shown: first, the substance of the basis; second, the inclusion within the ultimate reality; third, manifesting its non-obstruction; fourth, universal pervasion and harmonious fusion. The commentary explains:

Of the four gates above, the first is the gate of characteristics (*lakṣaṇa*), the second is the gate of signlessness (*animitta*), the third is the gate of the common teaching (*sāmānya-deśanā*), and the fourth is the gate of the distinct teaching. If the latter [the fourth] is applied to accord with the various vehicles, it encompasses the four types of non-obstruction; all are portions of the distinct teaching.)

The *Samantabhadra-caryā-nirdeśa* and the threefold contemplation of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) are identical in their underlying principle; this may be seen by examining them closely. If this is so, why is it not considered a commentary on the Dharma-realm of other sutras? Because its essential character is both vertical and horizontal, it cannot be fixed to a single standard. Therefore, the Patriarch said: "That which is the primary tenet of this sutra is the universal essence of all sutras."
The commentary states: Since it is said that "non-fusion constitutes sameness," it is evident that this is not a case where two distinct names are obliterated to become the same.
Furthermore, it is also clear that this Sameness Teaching (Tongjiao) One Vehicle synthesizes the Final and Sudden teachings (the above follows and confirms the *Sūtra Commentary*).
It is further said: "If self and other are mutually severed, then because one's own mind is of the same substance as the minds of all sentient beings, there is nothing outside of the mind.

Because the subject (the knower) and object (the known) are not destroyed, one is able to know. My own commentary states: This applies to both the Final and Sudden Teachings. However, the principle of being of the same substance belongs to the Sudden Teaching;
that which additionally maintains the meaning of not destroying the subject and object belongs to the Final Teaching. If one takes both [aspects] together, they are mutually severed.

The simultaneous existence of both [subject and object] is also perfect; this is the meaning of the "Common Teaching" (tóngjiào) within the doctrinal systems. The *Daśabhūmika-sūtra* states: "All are known as they truly are. The *Commentary* (Sù), fascicle 58, says: "Because one examines the facts of phenomena and perceives the reality of principle (*lǐ*).

Furthermore, it is not that one perceives dharmas outside the mind, nor is it that there is no object to be known. If self and other are mutually transcended, then one’s mind is of the same essence as the minds of sentient beings; thus, there is nothing 'outside the mind. Because the subject and object are not destroyed, there is the capacity to know. Moreover, the 'minds of others' is the general [category], while the rest are the particulars.

This is the true knowledge of the One Vehicle, wherein the six aspects (*liùxiàng*) are perfectly interfused. The *Chāo*, fascicle 41, states: "From 'all are known as they truly are' onwards, this is a general explanation of the meaning of 'knowing as they truly are. There are five levels of doctrinal intent. The first is common to the Hīnayāna and the Initial Teaching; its reality of principle applies generally to persons."

1. "Because the dharmas are empty of both [self and phenomena]" (*dvaya-śūnyatvāt*). This refers to the section beginning with "the two are also not outside the mind," which applies to both the Initial and Final Teachings; for the meaning of *vijñapti-mātra* (consciousness-only) is common to both teachings. 2. "If self and other are mutually severed. This applies to both the Final and Sudden Teachings.

When their characteristics are identical as one essence, this is the Sudden Teaching. When it additionally adopts the meaning of the non-destruction of the knower and the known, this is the Final Teaching. Furthermore, taking the totality of both severance and both existence constitutes the meaning of the Common Teaching within the Perfect [Teaching]. 3. "Moreover, the 'other-mind' is the totality...

This refers to the sixfold circular fusion (*ṣaḍ-lakṣaṇa-saṃpuṭa*), which belongs exclusively to the Distinct Teaching of the One Vehicle Common Teaching. **Explanation:** Regarding the classification according to the teachings, it is said that there are five types of teaching-intents and so forth. However, if considered in terms of mutual interpenetration, they are all the Distinct Teaching.

The critique states: Since it is called "comprehensive inclusion" (*zǒngqǔ*), it must encompass both teachings. Furthermore, within the Perfect Teaching (*yuánjiào*), this is the ultimate "non-separate" *tóng* (common/shared) teaching;
it is like the river water contained within the ocean—how could it not be salty? It is precisely identical to the "Common One Vehicle" (*tóngjiào yīshèng*) found here [in China]. [Question]:

The cited text may be so, but among the four types of "common" teachings, the *Tàn xuán* (Probing the Profundity) classifies them as branching out from the "shared" (*gòngjiào*) teaching. How can this also be the "common" within the Perfect Teaching? [Answer]: Taìyī says: It is for the purpose of establishing the Universal Dharma (*pǔfǎ*).

[This is] what is accomplished. In the *Dharmatā-śāstra*, there are three stages of entry into the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*). Although the teachings such as the *Lotus Sūtra* are not identical to the Perfect [Teaching], why did Guishan say: "If one speaks in terms of sudden opening, upon awakening to this point, one immediately enters the Perfect Teaching"?
The Secret Patriarch’s commentary on the meaning of the subject and object of realization states: "The non-duality of subject and object is the Final Teaching (Zhongjiao) of the Mahāyāna.
The simultaneous subsiding of both subject and object is the Path of Realization (Zhengdao) within the Sudden Teaching (Dunjiao) of the Mahāyāna" (*Yuanchao*, Vol. 2, Part 2).

Guǎnzǔ said: "When the subject and object are clearly distinct, one realizes the Dharma-realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*). When the subject and object are of a single aspect, one realizes the Dharma-realm of principle.

Furthermore, through the gate of the mutual identity of the unimpeded nature of phenomenon and principle, when both subject and object are extinguished, one realizes the gate of the unimpeded interpenetration of phenomenon and principle where forms are subsumed and have no fixed locus.
When existence and non-existence are unimpeded, one fully realizes the gate of the unobstructed nature of phenomenon and principle. This is the realization of the total inclusion within the One."

The "Non-dual" refers to the Shared Teaching (*sādhāraṇa-yāna*) as opposed to the Distinct Teaching (*pratyeka-yāna*). Thus, that which belongs to the Sudden is the Real; that which belongs to the Three is the Expedient (*upāya*), while that which belongs to the One is the Real.

This is to depart from the partial and unite with the Perfect. Indeed, within the ocean of teachings, there are many skillful means to guide the capacities of sentient beings, and the enumerations of phrases differ.
The various masters of former generations each expounded a single gate (as seen in the various systems for establishing the teachings), such as the Five Patriarchs.

They are encompassed and woven together to form a net of teachings; thus, there is opening and closing. Even if many teachings are established, they are all instances of the initial Perfect [teaching] being gradually opened up from within the Middle [teaching].

If this is so, then is it not the case that the Perfect [teaching] begins as the Small [Vehicle]? Answer: It is indeed so. This is the general in relation to the particular. Furthermore, how could one separate the partial and merge it with the Perfect?
This is because sentient capacities (mārga) are both universal and particular, and wisdom is threefold or unitary; since their attainments and orientations differ, [the distinctions arise].

Therefore, its unfolding and rolling back are not said to be of a single aspect. Unfolding while always being rolled back, and rolling back while immediately being unfolded—this sovereign freedom of unfolding and rolling back constitutes the great principle of the *Avataṃsaka* teaching-net.
